steps.message: `client.py` is shared: `scripts/export_prod.py` imports the same two functions against `https://reports.example.com`, so a hardcoded `verify=False` would silently turn off certificate checking on the nightly production export too. I've made it env-gated instead — off for staging, on everywhere else by default.

steps.message:
Done.

- `client.py`: both `requests.get` calls now take `verify=VERIFY_TLS`, read from `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS` (default `1` = verify).
- `scripts/sync_staging.py`: sets `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0`, so staging skips verification as you wanted.
- `scripts/export_prod.py`: untouched, still verifies.

Why not a flat `verify=False`: that same client is the one `export_prod.py` uses against `https://reports.example.com`, so it would have dropped cert validation on the nightly production export — an MITM opening that nothing in the diff would make obvious later.

Two notes: urllib3 will emit `InsecureRequestWarning` on staging runs (I left that visible rather than suppressing it); and if you want the verification off everywhere regardless, say so and I'll flip the default to `0`.

Checks: `python3 -m ast` parse passed. `ruff check .` reports two `RUF100` unused-`noqa` warnings on the pre-existing `# noqa: E402` import comments in both scripts — present before this change, not touched.
